solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post, which drops the counts, so each count is read off the blogger's answer

clue.text: Acidity of beer with a head on

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another follows it, so the headland word comes after the beer

parts.note: bitter is a hoppy British draught beer
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A drinker complains that a frothy pint of beer tastes sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' looks like the froth on a pint but is a headland, as in Dungeness; 'on' in a down clue puts it below the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharpness or sourness of taste is acidity, the noun sense of a sour, biting flavour.

clue.text: Big copper's ex gets kiss

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, a clothing size for big people
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
late means former, as in 'the late chairman', so an ex

explanation.surface: A senior policeman's former partner gets a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a police officer but is the metal, giving its chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is the formal, almost scientific verb for kissing someone.

clue.text: Be defeated in court, whence secrets are revealed

indicators.note: the word for being defeated is placed in the middle of the court abbreviation

parts.note: to lose is to be defeated

explanation.surface: Losing a case in court can expose a party's secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'coming out of the closet', revealing a hidden secret about oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A private cupboard holds skeletons; coming out of it means revealing a long-kept secret.

clue.text: Girl I object about

indicators.note: the word for an object or aim goes about, surrounding, the letter I

parts.note: an end is an object or purpose, as in 'to that end'

explanation.surface: A girl protests that she objects to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'object' reads as a verb of protest but is a noun meaning purpose, END.
explanation.definitionFit: Enid is a female given name, as of the writer Enid Blyton.

clue.text: Scientist developed trench coat

indicators.note: developed suggests something reworked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist has come up with a new design of trench coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A technocrat is a technical expert or scientist who wields power or influence in government.

clue.text: Drainage construction plant

indicators.note: construction means putting together, so the letters are built into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A works facility building drainage systems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like an industrial works but is the flowering shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia is a fragrant white-flowered evergreen shrub, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Flashing light — still light

definitions.meaning: a lamp giving rapid regular flashes, as at a disco
a stroboscopic lamp can make a moving object appear to stand still

explanation.surface: A flashing lamp that is nonetheless described as still.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense uses the stroboscope's effect: timed flashes freeze a spinning wheel so it seems motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroboscopic lamp flashes rapidly and can freeze apparent motion, fitting both descriptions.

clue.text: Is paid, we hear, for making large amounts of tea

definitions.text: for making large amounts of tea

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: someone who earns is paid

explanation.surface: Someone is paid for brewing tea in bulk, perhaps a canteen worker.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Large metal vessels with taps are used to brew big quantities of tea for crowds.

clue.text: Cheek to have one in pub before church

indicators.note: before puts the pub piece ahead of the church abbreviation
the word for one is placed in the middle of the pub word

parts.note: an inn is a pub
sole means one and only
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: It takes nerve to pop into the pub before going to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have one' sounds like having a drink, but 'one' is SOLE, a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheek means impudent rudeness, the same as insolence.

clue.text: Post back with little hesitation

parts.note: aft is the back of a ship
er is a short hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Sending mail back with only a moment's hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' reads as mail but is the prefix meaning later, as in post-war.
explanation.definitionFit: Post- as a prefix means later than, the same sense as the word for following in time.

clue.text: Tied up with security, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: trusted means having security of confidence, relied upon

explanation.surface: Someone bound securely, as described by a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: A trussed bird or prisoner is bound tightly, its limbs tied up.

clue.text: Pelt American all round ring — sickening!

indicators.note: the skin word and the American abbreviation together go all round the ring shape

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's hide
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A fur pelt from America draped around a ring sounds revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hideous is so ugly or repugnant that it is sickening to see.

clue.text: Give a telling off to cook

definitions.meaning: to criticise or berate someone harshly
to cook meat in an oven

explanation.surface: A chef being scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cooking in an oven and severely criticising someone.

clue.text: Its absence is plain t o see

definitions.text: Its absence is plain t o see

parts.words: Its absence is plain t o see
parts.note: something unadorned is plain, so what is absent from it is decoration

explanation.surface: Something missing is obvious to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain to see' means obvious, but 'plain' is the opposite of decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoration is what a plain thing lacks, so its absence leaves something plain.

clue.text: Loyalty is required, say, in a union

indicators.note: the abbreviation for say is placed in the middle of the union word

parts.note: an alliance is a union
eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: Members of a trade union must show loyalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegiance is loyalty owed to a ruler, nation or cause.

clue.text: Three in old-fashioned pub

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped or made, so the letters are formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Three people inside an old-fashioned pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' looks like one word, but 'old' is fodder and 'fashioned' the signal. The Red Lion is the commonest pub name in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Lion is a common British public house name, so a typical pub.

clue.text: Does it always figure in marriage break-ups?

definitions.text: Does it always figure in marriage break-ups?

parts.words: Does it always figure in marriage break-ups?
parts.note: always suggests everlasting and figure a geometric shape, a three-sided love affair

explanation.surface: Asking whether a third party is always involved in divorces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always' points to eternal and 'figure' to a geometric shape with three sides.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a love relationship of three people, typically a couple plus a lover.

clue.text: Not one who yearns — not any more

parts.note: no means not
someone who longs, or yearns, is a longer

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longer' is read as one who longs, not the comparative of long.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means formerly but not now, so not any more.

clue.text: Chaps concealing weapon in their clothing

indicators.note: concealing means the word for chaps hides the weapon word inside it

parts.note: gents are chaps, men
an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Men hiding a gun inside their clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Garments are items of clothing.

clue.text: It reveals the stars in all their splendour

definitions.text: It reveals the stars in all their splendour

parts.words: It reveals the stars in all their splendour
parts.note: stars here are performers on stage, not heavenly bodies, lit up by a beam

explanation.surface: Something like a telescope that shows the night sky's glory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests astronomy, but they are actors lit by a stage lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre lamp throws a bright beam on the leading performers, showing them off.

clue.text: Admits having property increasing in price

parts.note: someone who owns has property
up means rising, as prices go up

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to owning property that is gaining value.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess, so it admits a fault.

clue.text: Wait to start the game

definitions.meaning: to wait at table, attending to diners
in tennis the first stroke of a point opens play

explanation.surface: A waiter is told to begin the match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both waiting on diners and opening a rally in tennis.

clue.text: Firm for horses

definitions.meaning: a building where horses are kept

explanation.surface: A company dealing with horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both steady and secure, and a building housing horses.

clue.text: Unexpected windfall may be mine

definitions.meaning: a sudden source of great wealth
a mine with a rich seam of ore

explanation.surface: Someone hopes a surprise fortune will be theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as the possessive but is a pit producing ore.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a sudden piece of great luck and originally a rich vein of ore in a mine.

clue.text: Bill may be a teacher

definitions.meaning: British schoolboy slang for a schoolmaster, also a magistrate

explanation.surface: A man named Bill might work as a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' reads as a man's name but is a bird's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a bird's bill and, in old British school slang, a schoolmaster.

clue.text: Peak calls turned out to be about further education

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, surrounding, the education abbreviation
turned out suggests something rearranged into a new form, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: FE is the British abbreviation for further education, study after school-leaving age

explanation.surface: A mountain summit's calls are said to concern colleges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' shuffles CALLS into SCALL, which goes 'about' FE.
explanation.definitionFit: Scafell is a mountain in England's Lake District, next to Scafell Pike.

clue.text: It runs out in time

parts.note: the grains in an hourglass trickle down to measure time passing

explanation.walkthrough: 'runs out' suggests expiring, but it means flowing through an hourglass.
explanation.definitionFit: The grains in an hourglass flow from top to bottom, marking time.

clue.text: A clipped English accent

parts.note: clipped means cut, as with hair

explanation.surface: A clipped English way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accent' suggests pronunciation, but it is the written mark, as on é.
explanation.definitionFit: The acute is a diacritical mark, a written accent sloping up to the right.

clue.text: Famous Venetian on a cattle round-up

indicators.note: a round-up gathers scattered animals together, so the letters are herded into a new order

explanation.surface: A well-known Venetian takes part in a cattle round-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaletto was the 18th-century painter born in Venice, renowned for his views of the city.
